host: node packages/wasm-clang/test/run-cc.mjs --tarball <package.tgz> [--layout flat|pnpm|shared] [--expect old] [--kernel <spec>]: the package's wasixcc (bin/cc → clang + wasm-ld in bin/llvm.wasm) compiles wasix-sysroot's test/r18.c, r21.c, r24.c, r24link.c, r26.c, r27.c, r28.c and r28w.c inside slicc-kernel's Node entry against the wasix-sysroot the tarball pins (sysroot-exnref-eh), found through the package's own slicc.env (no WASIXCC_SYSROOT_PREFIX / CLANG_RESOURCE_DIR from the cert), installed as npm (flat) or a `pnpm add -g` project (pnpm) puts it, and the programs run there under users 'enforce' with the sysroot's own test/*.mjs specs. From 24.0.0-15 the glue runs as shipped: its appended Node-host runner stays out of a host that sets noInitialRun, as slicc-kernel's Node process worker does (glue-node-runner.patch, homescoop#276); older glues (--expect old, and wasm-binaryen's until it ships the guard) are cut off before the runner in the cert's copy only. The realm has no grep: cc's Asyncify check reads the import section with od (homescoop#451). ladder-pr runs every `ci` command after host-build.
checklist: 24.0.0-12 (wasix-sysroot 2025.9.30-24, slicc-kernel 1.61.0, users enforce): every probe compiled in the kernel by the package's wasixcc carries slicc.libc = "wasix-sysroot 2025.9.30-24"

slicc.env WASIXCC_SYSROOT_PREFIX = ${package}/../wasix-sysroot finds the dependency in the flat npm layout (/node_modules/@ai-ecoverse/{wasm-clang,wasix-sysroot}) and in a `pnpm add -g` project (the two side by side in .pnpm/@ai-ecoverse+wasm-clang@<v>/node_modules/@ai-ecoverse/, the project's wasm-clang a symlink: the kernel resolves `..` physically); 24.0.0-11 hard-coded /shared/lib/node_modules/@ai-ecoverse/wasix-sysroot, which no package manager fills

r18: select with exceptfds, a 0.2 s select timeout that waits, pselect with only exceptfds, physical chdir(..), POSIX TZ (EST5EDT, CET-1CEST, <+0530>), socketpair SOCK_NONBLOCK|SOCK_CLOEXEC, sigaction SA_RESETHAND / SIG_IGN / a kill(getpid()) handler
r21: in a 100x30 pty, isatty and TIOCGWINSZ 100x30, cfmakeraw reads ^C as byte 3 with no SIGINT, TCSAFLUSH restores; pipes and files ENOTTY, a closed fd EBADF
r24: chown / lchown / fchown / fchownat and stat owners as root and as kernel user cone (EPERM giving files away, chgrp to the own supplementary group)
r24link: link / linkat with AT_FDCWD (relative and absolute), AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW and a dirfd on either side link the same inode on a tmpfs mount
negative (--expect old): wasm-clang 24.0.0-11 (wasix-sysroot 2025.9.30-17) builds r24 with no slicc.libc marker, and as root under users enforce chown to a real id is -1 ENOSYS

24.0.0-14 (wasix-sysroot 2025.9.30-28, slicc-kernel 1.93.0, users enforce, R28_KERNEL_MASK=1 R28_WINDOW=1): probes compiled in the kernel carry slicc.libc "wasix-sysroot 2025.9.30-28"; r28 (pthread_sigmask/sigprocmask through slicc.sigmask_set: a blocked SIGUSR1 pending, delivered on unblock, SIGKILL/SIGSTOP unblockable, per-thread masks, fork and exec keep the mask; the package's cc asyncifies it with wasm-binaryen's wasm-opt since it imports proc_fork) and r28w (pselect/ppoll/sigsuspend through slicc.sigmask_poll: pending-at-call EINTR, sigsuspend wakes, gpg-agent's pselect(sigmask) HUP/TERM and ssh's ppoll(osigset) INT at once, the arrived-before-wait window ends the next wait at once, sigtimedwait/sigwaitinfo/sigwait ENOSYS) pass with r18, r21, r24, r26 and r27 in the flat layout (wasm-binaryen next to wasm-clang, as npm puts the dependency, and wasm-grep in the realm: the cc driver finds proc_fork with grep); r24link runs on slicc-kernel 1.83.0 (linkat AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW on tmpfs is ENOSYS from 1.84.0 on, a kernel regression with the Kernel Coordinator); the pnpm layout runs r18, r21, r24, r26, r27 (no wasm-opt on PATH there, so no fork probes). 24.0.0-13 (wasix-sysroot -27): r28w does not link (undefined symbol ppoll), NEGATIVE.md

24.0.0-15 (packaging-only: -11's bytes, homescoop#276 and #451): every glue of the package (bin/llvm and its 11 byte-copies) carries the noInitialRun-guarded Node-host runner, and clang, wasm-ld and llvm-nm --version run through the shipped glue on slicc-kernel's Node entry (24.0.0-14, glue as shipped: 'clang: error: no input files', rc 70, on slicc-kernel 1.44.0-1.92.0; 1.93.0's Node lockdown hides process, so the runner can't fire there, and the ci entry on 1.92.0 (r18, flat) is the one that shows the guard working); the realm has no grep (wasm-grep is no longer in needs), and cc asyncifies exactly the probes that import wasix_32v1.proc_fork / stack_checkpoint / stack_restore (r28, r28w), which pass; the others stay unasyncified. 24.0.0-14 without grep: r28.wasm imports proc_fork but comes out unasyncified (NEGATIVE.md)

24.0.0-16 (packaging-only, homescoop#692): cc's Asyncify step also runs for a link without -o (a.out) and for the joined -oFILE: r28 built as wasixcc -O2 r28.c and with -or28j.wasm comes out asyncified, WASIXCC_ASYNCIFY=0 leaves it unasyncified, and wasixcc --version next to an a.out leaves it byte for byte. 24.0.0-17 (packaging-only, homescoop#710, #711): calls that write no program leave an a.out beside them byte for byte, an asyncified one and a non-wasm one: wasixcc --version, -v, -fsyntax-only r18.c, '-###' r18.c and a header-only x.h all exit 0. The driver adds its link libraries only when there are link inputs, and post-links only real links. 24.0.0-16: -fsyntax-only and -### re-ran Asyncify on the old a.out (rc 1), and -v ran a link of nothing that removed it (NEGATIVE.md)

24.0.0-18 (packaging-only, homescoop#721, #722, #711): the driver scans @response files one level deep, so their -o and inputs count (wasixcc -O2 @args.rsp with 'r28.c -o r28r.wasm' gives an asyncified r28r.wasm, and the a.out beside it is left alone); it post-links only an output this call wrote (cksum before and after) and only a wasm module (wasixcc -x c-header x.h -o x.pch exits 0 and leaves x.pch plain); the argument after -Xlinker -o is not the program (-O2 r28.c -Xlinker -o -Xlinker xl.wasm gives an asyncified a.out); and -B / -working-directory / -resource-dir values are not link inputs (wasixcc -v -B /tmp leaves the a.out). 24.0.0-17: -Xlinker -o left a.out unasyncified, and -v -B /tmp removed it (NEGATIVE.md)

24.0.0-19 (packaging-only; Codex on #725): a link that rewrites the same bytes still gets its post-link step (the output counts as written when it is newer than a marker made before the frontend, or its cksum changed): r28 -o r28n.wasm with WASIXCC_ASYNCIFY=0, then the same link without it, comes out asyncified; response files are read with quotes and nesting as clang reads them (@q.rsp with -o "sp ace.wasm", @outer.rsp naming @inner.rsp with r28.c -o nest.wasm: both asyncified), never evaluated when they hold shell syntax. 24.0.0-18: the same-bytes relink and the quoted output stay unasyncified (NEGATIVE.md)

24.0.0-20 (packaging-only, homescoop#754, #755): a response file with { } or ~ is split on blanks, never evaluated, so @brace.rsp (r28.c -o br{a,b}.wasm) gives an asyncified br{a,b}.wasm, the name clang writes; a failed compile next to an existing output leaves no wasix-out.* marker in TMPDIR. 24.0.0-19: br{a,b}.wasm unasyncified (NEGATIVE.md)

24.0.0-21 (packaging-only, homescoop#769): the driver reads response files with clang's GNU tokenizer rules, character by character and never through eval (blanks split; ' and " quote; backslash escapes in and out of quotes; empty quoted words count; a UTF-8 BOM is skipped), so a quoted -o next to { } ~ $, tabs, CRLF or backslash escapes names the file clang writes: @bq.rsp ('q {x}.wasm'), @dq.rsp (-DX=$Y … 'd o.wasm'), @esc.rsp ("e s'c~.wasm") and a 14.5 kB @long.rsp with 800 quoted words ('long {$L}.wasm') are all asyncified. 24.0.0-20: q {x}.wasm unasyncified (NEGATIVE.md)
